note: WP-49 adds two interactive tools and the /tools/ hub. Every formula, folder, item and statement in the new copy traces to a published page of this site, to a public reference page cited by URL (the six calculator results the research brief does not define), or is labelled below as an editorial choice. No amount, benchmark, target, seat count, price, date, statistic, person, company or testimonial is introduced. The entries map each block to its origin.

sources.title: Early-stage SaaS metrics: definitions and formulas, appendix formula table
sources.exact_url_or_locator: src/content/research/early-stage-saas-metrics-definitions.md, section 'Appendix: formula table and reporting checklist'
sources.next_review: Any change to the brief's formula table
sources.variables_units_scope: Three formulas are shown exactly as the brief's table publishes them: NRR ('[(Beginning recurring revenue - MRR lost from churn - MRR lost from downgrades + revenue from upgrades) / Beginning recurring revenue] x 100'), simple CAC ('MCC / CA') and CLV ('Margin x (Retention / (1 + Discount - Retention))'). The six other results are not defined in the brief and each cites a public page (the wp49-ref-* sources). The six-question reporting checklist on the calculator page is the brief's checklist.
sources.methodology_limitations: tests/unit/wp-49/formulas.test.ts parses the brief's table and checks each brief-sourced formula character for character, and checks that none of the six reference metrics appears in the brief. The brief gives no benchmarks and no target values, and neither does the calculator. The discount term in CLV is fixed at zero and the page says so.
sources.license_access_attribution: Internal; quoted from the site's own brief
sources.freshness_trigger: Any change to the brief's formula table or checklist

sources.title: How To Calculate MRR (Baremetrics Academy)
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: Net New MRR = New MRR + Expansion MRR - Churned MRR. The calculator lists downgrades as a separate Contraction MRR input and subtracts it, which gives the same total as the reference where churned MRR includes downgrades.
sources.methodology_limitations: The page is inconsistent about whether churned MRR includes downgrades (one section says cancellations or downgrades, a later one assigns downgrades to contraction). The calculator's input labels state which is which. A vendor explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how net new MRR is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: Revenue churn (net and gross revenue churn rate)
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: Gross MRR Churn Rate = (SUM of Churn & Contraction MRR) / (MRR at start of period). The calculator multiplies by 100 and shows a percent.
sources.methodology_limitations: Net revenue churn (expansion subtracted) is a different measure on the same page and is not used; NRR is taken from the research brief instead. A vendor explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how gross revenue churn is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: SaaS Quick Ratio
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: SaaS Quick Ratio = (New MRR + Expansion MRR) / (Churned MRR + Contraction MRR), with the same four component definitions the calculator uses.
sources.methodology_limitations: The page names 4.0 as a frequently cited target; the calculator and its page repeat no benchmark or target. The SaaS quick ratio is not the accounting acid-test ratio. A training-provider explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how the SaaS quick ratio is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: CAC Payback Period
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: CAC Payback Period = Sales and Marketing Expense / (New MRR x Gross Margin), in months. The page's worked example divides both sides by the customers acquired (CAC / (average new MRR per customer x gross margin)), which is the per-customer form the calculator uses.
sources.methodology_limitations: The reference uses sales and marketing expense; the calculator uses whatever acquisition spend the founder enters and says to label which form it is. Churn during the payback months is ignored. A training-provider explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how CAC payback is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: LTV/CAC Ratio
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: LTV/CAC Ratio = Lifetime Value (LTV) / Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC). LTV in the calculator is the research brief's CLV formula; CAC is the brief's simple CAC.
sources.methodology_limitations: The page also states a 3.0x benchmark and thresholds; none is repeated by the calculator or its page. A training-provider explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how the ratio of lifetime value to CAC is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: Cash Runway Explained
sources.next_review: Before release, or when the page changes or is removed
sources.variables_units_scope: Cash Runway = Current Cash Balance / Monthly Net Burn Rate. Net burn is the founder's own input (cash out less cash in over a month).
sources.methodology_limitations: Assumes this month's burn repeats; arithmetic, not a forecast. A training-provider explainer, not a standard.
sources.license_access_attribution: Linked, not copied. Used to cite how runway is commonly calculated; the page says it is a convention and not a WE method.
sources.freshness_trigger: The reference page changing its formula, or going offline

sources.title: Suggested stage for each evidence-room item
sources.exact_url_or_locator: src/components/islands/we-evidence-room/items.ts, the stage of each row and READINESS_STAGE
sources.variables_units_scope: Neither guide ranks items by company stage. The stage on each item is WE's own suggested order for gathering evidence, using the three of the four published stage labels (Idea or prototype, First product, Early customer evidence). The fourth stage, 'Several products, or a regulated field', has no filter of its own: the page tells that company to show all items and ask its own counsel what else applies.
sources.methodology_limitations: Editorial sequencing. The page labels it 'a suggestion, not an investor requirement' and does not claim any investor asks for items in this order.
sources.freshness_trigger: Any change to the stage labels in src/components/pricing/stages.ts

sources.title: What each tool does with the visitor's input
sources.variables_units_scope: 'Your numbers stay on this page' (calculator: nothing saved, sent or placed in the address) and 'your ticks are kept in the part of the address after the # sign' (evidence room: no storage, no cookie, no request) restate what the code does. The e2e specs record every request after the page loads and fail on any, and read local storage, session storage and cookies after use.
sources.methodology_limitations: The evidence-room address holds the ticks, so anyone given the address sees them; the page says so.
sources.freshness_trigger: Any change that adds storage or a request
